**Short answer:** A module declares its schema by calling `defineConfigSchema(moduleName, schema)` from `@openmrs/esm-framework`, usually in `startupApp()`. Each config key is an object with `_type`, `_default` and `_description`. Implementers then override those defaults through their configuration, which is what the schema validates. I did not read the implementer-side override mechanism itself; the docs point to the Configure O3 guide for that, so treat the override step as documented but not verified in code here.

**Documentation**

- `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs/content/en-US/docs/configuration-system.mdx` is the main guide. It covers designing the schema (lines 25–48), defining it with `_type`/`_default`/`_description` (lines 50–100), typing (lines 102–110 and 307–329), and registering it in `startupApp()` (lines 277–301). It also explains the reserved `Display conditions` and `Translation overrides` keys that every module gets automatically.
- `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs/content/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/overview.mdx` (lines 201–221) shows `defineConfigSchema(moduleName, configSchema)` called from `startupApp()` in `src/index.ts`.
- The recipe and migration guides repeat the same pattern (`recipes/add-a-left-panel-to-o3.mdx` 131–145, `migration-guides/migrate-to-core-v5.mdx` 564–570).

**Implementation (openmrs-esm-core)**

- `packages/framework/esm-config/src/module-config/module-config.ts`:
  - `defineConfigSchema` (lines 369–378) validates the schema, merges it with the implicit schema, and stores it under the module name.
  - `implicitConfigSchema` (lines 1295–1308) holds the reserved keys.
  - `getConfig` (lines 518–524) returns the resolved config with the reserved keys stripped.
  - `defineExtensionConfigSchema` (line 445) is the extension-level variant.
  - `mergeDeepReplace` (line 42) and `validateConfigSchema` (line 884) do the merge and validation. I only saw their starting lines, so the ranges are approximate.
- Mock versions of `defineConfigSchema` exist in `packages/framework/esm-config/mock.ts` and `mock-jest.ts`. They are test helpers, not the real implementation.

Falkon rejected the bare name `openmrs-esm-core` for one search and accepted the full `github.com/openmrs/...` form, so I used that form for those calls.
